message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 240, "amount_cents": 8145}, {"order_id": 243, "amount_cents": 13498}, {"order_id": 245, "amount_cents": 10428}]
Refunds requested in this batch (from the batch order, signed by Alpha): [{"order_id": 240, "amount_cents": 8145}, {"order_id": 243, "amount_cents": 13498}, {"order_id": 245, "amount_cents": 10428}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: The handoff says the refunds were applied and they match the signed batch. Before paying anyone, I need the order list to see which customers are in this batch.
The handoff's refund claims need checking against the shared ledger before any payout is recorded. I'll pull the refunds list and compare it with the applied and requested amounts.

The refunds list matches the handoff's applied and signed amounts, and each refund is within its order's amount. Next I'll get the net balance for the first customer, acme, rather than computing it myself.
Acme's net balance of 7125 matches the order totals minus the applied refunds (28768 - 21643). Next I'll get the net balance for birch, the second customer in the batch.
Acme and birch are checked. The last customer in the batch is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself.
All three customers' net balances match the order totals minus the verified refunds: acme 7125, birch 55306, cobalt 28827. No discrepancies, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 55306 matches its order totals (36544 + 18762) with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch payouts are recorded. The last customer is cobalt, whose net balance of 28827 matches its orders (18183 + 21072) minus the 10428 refund on order 245. I'll record that payout.
All three payouts are recorded and each net balance matched the order totals minus the verified refunds, so the batch is complete.
